body.statement: On every fixed graph box in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), all count moments are finite uniformly over the box; the joint mass function, every component PGF on \((0,1)^p\), and every fixed truncated-factorization contrast are twice continuously differentiable in the coefficients, with differentiation permitted term by term.  For each fixed graph tuple, the coefficient-to-law map is injective and has injective differential at every coefficient vector.  The compact law images of two distinct graph tuples are disjoint.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a graph tuple \(\boldsymbol d\).  It is enough to argue one type at a time, because its joint mass is a factor in the type product and the parameter blocks of distinct types are disjoint.  Choose a topological ordering of the vertices.  At a root, every moment of \(V_s\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\alpha_s)\) is a polynomial in \(\alpha_s\), hence is bounded uniformly on the compact coefficient box.  Suppose the claim is known for all predecessors of a non-root \(s\).  Conditional on its parents,
\[
\mathbb E[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
=\sum_{k=0}^m
\left\{\begin{matrix}m\\k\end{matrix}\right\}
\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})^k .
\]
The rate is a polynomial in predecessor counts with coefficients bounded on the box.  Expanding its powers and applying Holder's inequality bounds every displayed expectation by finitely many predecessor moments.  Induction gives, for every integer \(m\geq0\),
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}\mathbb E_\theta
\left(\sum_{s=1}^pV_s\right)^m<\infty. \tag{1}
\]
The same induction applies after fixing one intervention coordinate at either \(1\) or \(2\).

Every rate has a uniform positive lower bound.  If \(t\) indexes the intercept or one edge coefficient in the conditional rate of node \(s\), put
\[
a_{st}(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
\in\{1,v_k^{q_{sk}}:k\in\operatorname{pa}(s)\}.
\]
For the positive joint mass \(p_\theta(v)\),
\[
\partial_t\log p_\theta(v)
=a_{st}(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
\left\{\frac{v_s}{\lambda_s(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})}-1\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
First and second derivatives of \(p_\theta(v)\) are therefore \(p_\theta(v)\) times functions bounded uniformly by a fixed polynomial in \(v\).  Equation (1) supplies a summable uniform majorant, first on a slightly larger positive coefficient box and then on the given compact box.  Dominated convergence consequently permits two termwise derivatives of the mass, PGF, intervened mass, and the two contrast expectations.  It also gives their continuity.

The observational law identifies its positive conditional masses at every parent vector, hence identifies
\[
\lambda_s(x)=\mathbb E_\theta[V_s\mid
V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}=x].
\]
Evaluating at \(x=0\) gives \(\alpha_s\), and evaluating at the parent vector having coordinate \(k\) equal to \(1\) and all other coordinates zero gives
\[
b_{sk}=\lambda_s(e_k)-\lambda_s(0).
\]
Thus the parameter-to-law map is injective within a fixed graph.

For differential injectivity, collect the node-\(s\) scores from (2) into
\[
S_s=f_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
\frac{V_s-\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})}
{\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})},
\qquad
f_s=(1,(V_k^{q_{sk}})_{k\in\operatorname{pa}(s)})^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Along the topological filtration these are martingale differences.  Hence different node blocks are orthogonal, and the information block is
\[
I_s=\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
\frac{f_sf_s^{\mathsf T}}{\lambda_s}\right]. \tag{3}
\]
If \(c^{\mathsf T}I_sc=0\), positivity of the joint mass implies \(c^{\mathsf T}f_s(x)=0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}(s)|}\).  Evaluation at zero and then with one coordinate equal to \(1\) forces every coordinate of \(c\) to vanish.  Thus (3) is positive definite, and every nonzero parameter direction \(a\) has \(\mathbb E_\theta[(a^{\mathsf T}S)^2]>0\).

Suppose its directional PGF derivative vanished on a nonempty open box in \((0,1)^p\).  It is the absolutely convergent signed power series
\[
\sum_{v\in\mathbb N_0^p}p_\theta(v)
a^{\mathsf T}S(v)z^v. \tag{4}
\]
Successive one-variable power-series uniqueness shows every coefficient in (4) is zero.  For completeness, an absolutely convergent one-variable power series that is zero on an open subinterval has all Taylor derivatives zero at every interior point; its Taylor expansion therefore vanishes on the overlapping interval of convergence, and finitely many overlapping intervals continue the equality to every compact subinterval of \((0,1)\).  After continuation down to zero, division by the least nonzero power and passage to zero rules out a nonzero coefficient.  Fixing the other coordinates and iterating this argument over the \(p\) coordinates proves the multivariate assertion.  This contradicts the strictly positive variance just obtained.  The differential is therefore injective.

Finally, the proposition on polynomial-class inclusion and the cited CPCM DAG-identification lemma imply that two different labeled graph tuples cannot generate the same law.  Continuity proved above sends compact coefficient boxes to compact law images, so those distinct images are disjoint compact sets.  All assertions also hold after stacking the finitely many types.
